artworks.title: The Hestia Giustiniani
artworks.artist: Roman copy after a Greek original
artworks.description: A marble statue of the veiled goddess of the hearth, a Roman copy after an early Classical Greek original of about 470 BC in the Severe style. The heavy peplos, grave frontal stance and modestly drawn veil convey Hestia's austere domestic dignity. The statue takes its name from the Giustiniani collection in Rome, where it was long held.

artworks.title: The Hestia Tapestry
artworks.description: A wool tapestry woven in Byzantine Egypt in the sixth century AD, now in the Dumbarton Oaks collection in Washington, DC. It shows the goddess enthroned as Hestia Polyolbos, 'Hestia rich in blessings', flanked by attendants bearing medallions inscribed with the gifts she bestows. It is a rare survival of the pagan goddess's imagery from a Christianizing age.

artworks.title: Fresco of Vesta-Hestia from a Pompeian lararium
artworks.description: A lararium fresco from Pompeii (VII 12 11) depicting Vesta — the Roman form of Hestia — as the goddess of the domestic hearth, the quiet centre of household cult. Painted for a private shrine rather than a public temple, it shows how the Greek goddess of the sacred fire lived on in Roman domestic religion: the same veiled, matronly presence who received the first and last offerings of every sacrifice, here keeping watch over a Campanian house.

artworks.title: Hestia, Goddess of the Hearth and Domesticity
artworks.description: A wood engraving of Hestia published in August Heinrich Petiscus's popular mythology handbook Der Olymp oder die Mythologie der Griechen und Römer (Leipzig, 1878). The veiled goddess stands with a torch and a bowl, the Victorian schoolroom's canonical image of the hearth deity — austere, unwed, and absent from the flashier Olympian quarrels — through which nineteenth-century readers first met the quietest of the Twelve.

popCulture.title: Hades II
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Hestia joins Supergiant's Olympian roster as the goddess of the hearth: flame boons and domestic steel for Melinoë — a rare modern starring turn for the quietest Olympian.

popCulture.title: Vesta (mythology)
popCulture.description: Roman Vesta carries Hestia into the Forum — the eternal hearth, the Vestal virgins, and the city's sacred fire under another name.

popCulture.title: Hestia
popCulture.description: Hestia remains the quiet centre of the Greek house — the first and last offering, the goddess who never left the hearth for Olympus' quarrels.

popCulture.title: Hestia (character)
popCulture.creator: Fujino Ōmori
popCulture.description: Ōmori's DanMachi Hestia is the Greek hearth goddess transplanted into a fantasy city — breakout cosplay icon and the rare modern character who is Hestia, not merely named after her.

popCulture.title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians
popCulture.creator: Rick Riordan
popCulture.description: Riordan gives Hestia the Last Olympian's quiet climax: the goddess of the hearth who refused a throne so the fire at the centre of Olympus would never go out.

films.title: Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon?
films.description: The anime adaptation of Fujino Ōmori's light novels makes Hestia a co-lead: the goddess of the hearth descended to Orario, binding a familia around a single Adventurer — the quiet Olympian as a modern starring role.

films.title: Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon?: Arrow of the Orion
films.description: The theatrical DanMachi film keeps Hestia at the emotional centre of Bell's quest — the hearth goddess whose blessing and worry travel with him into a mythic dungeon crisis.

films.title: Blood of Zeus
films.description: The Netflix saga gives Hestia a rare screen turn among the Olympians — entrusted with Olympus's hidden stone, the hearth goddess as keeper of what must not fall into Titan hands.

music.title: La vestale (Spontini)
music.description: Spontini's Napoleonic grand opera turns on the eternal flame of Vesta: a priestess who lets the hearth go dark for love — Hestia's Roman cult as the stage for vow, fire and pardon.

music.title: La vestale (Mercadante)
music.description: Mercadante's Neapolitan tragedia lirica returns to Vesta's temple: a vestal who lets the sacred flame die for love — Hestia's Roman cult as bel canto catastrophe.
